answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to crack open a walnut of real work before earning trust: a small, verifiable task bonded by stake and reviewed by random peers. Reputation then grows slowly, like velvet wearing soft with use, never bought in bulk. The fable of a thousand fake agents collapses once every identity must pay in effort and time, because sybil farms cannot fake sustained, peer-checked history at scale.
